input.title: fix-slugify-diacritics proposal
input.content:
# Proposal: fix-slugify-diacritics

## Intent
slugify('Crème Brûlée') returns 'crème-brûlée' instead of 'creme-brulee'. Root cause: src/slugify.js line 10 regex /[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu keeps accented letters, and there is no normalization step. Slugs should be ASCII-friendly for Latin diacritics (URL safety, consistency).

## Scope - In
- src/slugify.js: after toLowerCase/trim, apply .normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{M}+/gu, '') before the non-alphanumeric replace (Approach A).
- Regression tests in test/slugify.test.js: 'Crème Brûlée' -> 'creme-brulee'; 'Café Münster' -> 'cafe-munster'; precomposed vs decomposed input give equal output; 3 existing ASCII tests retained unchanged.
- Optional one-line README note (line 5 area) on diacritic handling.

## Scope - Out
- Non-decomposable letters (ß, ø, æ, œ, đ, ł) mapping (Approach B, possible follow-up).
- Non-Latin scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, etc.): behaviour unchanged (still kept).
- New dependencies (Approach C rejected).
- Any change to ASCII output, signature, or export shape.

## Approach
Approach A, adopted unattended with explorer assumptions: add a NFD normalization + combining-mark strip step in slugify. Zero deps, minimal diff (~1 line). Node>=26 supports String.prototype.normalize and \p{M}. Lowercasing before normalize is fine.

## Affected Areas
- /private/tmp/e-N0Ay1p/home/cwd/src/slugify.js
- /private/tmp/e-N0Ay1p/home/cwd/test/slugify.test.js
- /private/tmp/e-N0Ay1p/home/cwd/README.md (optional note)

## Risks
1. Non-decomposable letters (ß, ø, æ, ł) remain non-ASCII in slugs. Likelihood: High (for such inputs); Impact: Low; Mitigation: documented as out of scope, follow-up Approach B.
2. Non-Latin scripts still produce non-ASCII slugs, and stripping \p{M} could remove combining marks required by some scripts (e.g. Devanagari vowel signs, Thai), altering their slugs. Likelihood: Medium; Impact: Medium; Mitigation: design phase to consider restricting the strip to Latin-base marks (U+0300-036F) instead of all \p{M}; add a test documenting chosen behaviour.
3. Existing consumers relying on accented slugs get changed output. Likelihood: Low; Impact: Medium; Mitigation: note in README/changelog; existing slugs are regenerated only if callers recompute.
4. Unattended run: open questions (ß/ø/æ, non-Latin handling) were decided by assumption, not user input. Likelihood: Medium; Impact: Low; Mitigation: human review at proposal approval gate.

## Rollback Plan
Revert the single commit (git revert) restoring src/slugify.js and tests; no data migrations or dependencies involved. Slugs already persisted by callers are unaffected by the code revert.

## Success Criteria
1. slugify('Crème Brûlée') === 'creme-brulee' and slugify('Café Münster') === 'cafe-munster'.
2. NFC and NFD forms of the same input yield identical slugs.
3. The 3 existing ASCII tests ('Hello World', '  Rock & Roll!!  ', 'Top 10 Tips') pass unmodified.
4. Full test suite passes (npm test) with no new dependencies in package.json.
5. Diff limited to src/slugify.js, test/slugify.test.js (and optional README).
